prose.text: The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order. `capability-drift` runs before the default-features workspace nextest; the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen and the base-identity bindings close come last, since no procedure is added. The chunk's own entries come first: - the collection proof and the targeted pin run; - the regression run over `interpretation` + `xtask`; - the dev-host routing reading, after its example build; - the scope guard, the lockfile-package probe, and the source probes (no print site; no subprocess, dlopen or env   read).

Absences, each with its reason: - No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent. - No boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `observability.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `tauri.conf.json`,   `capabilities/*.json` — the scope guard proves it), so the boot smoke does not bind (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate). - There is no harness live leg and no self-verify. The routing reading is a re-runnable dev-host probe that binds no   port. - No package is added (`tempfile` is already in the lock), so `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not listed locally; the   CI `supply-chain` job runs them, and the operator CI read asserts it green.

The routing entry is HOST-DEPENDENT by design: it reads `…_CUDA_…` only on a host with one of the eight candidates (this dev host, measured). It is the chunk's dev-host evidence and is re-run by the wrap on the same host. It is never a CI gate; the host-independent guard is the pin set.

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on this Linux host, because it drives every stage through `wsl.exe` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs`). As in the predecessor chunks (founder deviation 2026-10-04), its six stages run NATIVELY by hand before the push: the six `operator` entries after hygiene, each in the stage isolation of `Linux::cmd`. - Stage 3 takes a fresh per-invocation `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` under `target/pre-push/`, and stage 6 a per-invocation   data dir, with no `rm` (founder rulings 2026-10-04). - Stage 5 re-emits the no-mcp bindings, so the regen and the base-identity close are RE-FIRED as `operator` entries   after stage 6, before the push.

ONE-SHOT controls at /implement, never listed, because they mutate source and revert: Step 1's red-before-green run and Step 6's mutation checks. The listed, non-mutating `cuda_probe_` entry guards the property on every re-run.
